source_semantics: Degree membership in the literal mask dict precedes coordinate indexing; accepted key types follow actual dict equality/hash, not an assumed exact-int API.
Circular means np.all(coords[0,:]==coords[-1,:]); NaN endpoints are not equal. Circular path drops last input row and uses convolve2d same; open path uses valid. Both use wrap boundaries.
Two 1xL masks are np.array(mask,float)/(2**degree), then convolve2d(coords.T,mask,mode=method,boundary=wrap) and transpose back.

Output begins as fresh np.zeros((even.shape[1]+odd.shape[1],2)) with default float64; even goes to indices1::2 and odd to0::2. Complex convolution casts to this float output before any later stacking.

Circular output closes with out[0,:]; preserve_ends is evaluated only after convolution/interleave, and if true with open input stacks original endpoints. That late stack can promote dtype, e.g. complex endpoints; canonical dtype/storage will be observed, not generalized blindly.

Minimum SciPy wrapper coerces in1/in2 with np.asarray, validates 2D, applies valid-mode swap check and mode/boundary encoding, then calls _sigtools._convolve2d(...flip=1...). Modern additionally selects an array namespace and wraps its return.

Official minimum C allocates output dimensions from same/valid and accumulates each tap in increasing k with a zero-initialized sum; no output-column iterations occur for same width0, so singleton circular slicing does not enter modulo-zero wrap arithmetic. Compiler contraction/modern binary details remain unproven until implementation review.

Ordinary decimal-coordinate degree1..7 and dtype/layout cases target full weighted B-spline arithmetic. Endpoint identity/mutation, warnings/errors/FP state and exact output words/layout are prospective capture evidence.
